title: Cross-border flow gating and customer permitlist runtime
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Customers require strict enforcement of data residency and region-only routing (e.g., EU-only) while some accounts need sanctioned exceptions (permitlist) or emergency passthroughs. Current router supports simple region preference but lacks a compact, testable precedence model combining customer-level allow/deny, plan-tier routing, capacity fallbacks, and safe emergency overrides.

Goals: 1) Define a deterministic policy evaluation order that is auditable and minimal-latency. 2) Implement a runtime adapter that enforces: EU-only routes, account-level permitlist and denylist, tier-based routing (hosted vs dedicated), and model-variant fallback rules (quantized / lower-capacity variants) while honoring residency constraints. 3) Provide observability (per-request decision trace) and emergency bypass with strong guardrails (timeboxed, audit-logged, revokable).

Design summary: We will introduce a compact policy DSL (Policy: {scope, constraint, precedence, emergency_action}) evaluated in four phases: 1) Account gating: read customer profile flags (residency_required, permit_exceptions, emergency_passthrough_allowed). 2) Static graph match: region availability + capacity tiers for the requested model family. 3) Business rules: account-level allowlist/denylist evaluation with explicit precedence tokens. 4) Fallback selection: if primary route violates residency, try compatible local variant; if unavailable, follow one of two behaviors based on account_policy: soft-fail (reject with 403) or graceful-fallback to remote variant (only if emergency_passthrough true and policy timeboxed).

Key decisions and rationale: - Precedence: Explicit denylist > residency constraint > account permitlist > tier preference > fallback policy. This is deliberate: a denylist must be able to hard-block traffic even if residency flags or permitlists exist. Permitlist entries are narrow and require justification in customer metadata. - Emergency passthrough must be opt-in per-account and require a short TTL and an operator-approved justification recorded in audit log. - Model-variant mapping: maintain a compatibility table that marks which variants satisfy jurisdictional constraints (e.g., on-prem shard, EU-hosted quantized copy). The router will prefer same-variant family first to preserve output fidelity.

Runtime implications: Policy evaluation must be O(1) additional lookups per request (cacheable per-account and per-route), with decision trace propagated in request headers for downstream tracing and logged to the console. We will implement strict caching with invalidation hooks on account changes to avoid stale allow/deny enforcement.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests for precedence, property-based tests for policy combinations, and e2e against a staging mesh simulating regional capacity failures. Rollout plan: feature-flagged start in Canary for a small set of accounts, then gradual % rollout, with automated rollback if customer error rate or policy-mismatch metrics exceed SLOs.

Acceptance criteria and metrics are below.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic evaluation order implemented and documented
Per-request decision trace emitted and visible in Console logs
Account-level permitlist and denylist enforced with cache invalidation on updates
Emergency passthrough gated by TTL and operator justification, audit-log entries created
Fallback to compatible model variant respects residency constraints unless emergency passthrough is active
Integration tests covering at least 12 policy permutations pass in CI
